#5379. Paraguay Bank Collapse Shows Why Bitcoin Was Created as USDT Hits Premium

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Paraguay bank crisis is showing why Bitcoin was created in the first place. USDT sellers reportedly demanded premiums of up to 13% after authorities placed major digital lender Ueno Bank into resolution.

MILLIONS of people LOCKED OUT of their own money as Ueno bank COLLAPSES IN Paraguay President Pena faces IMPEACHMENT — reports pic.twitter.com/3vb8z7MIQm

The crisis left 3 million customers temporarily unable to access their accounts. Some peer-to-peer (P2P) listings showed Tether’s USDT trading around 6,942 Paraguayan guaraníes. That compared with the central bank’s November 4 dollar reference of 6,144.02 guaraníes.

The USDT premium shows growing demand for dollar-denominated assets outside conventional banking. It also revives a question that shaped Bitcoin’s creation: what happens when people cannot freely access money held inside financial institutions?

The Central Bank of Paraguay initiated Ueno Bank’s resolution process on November 3. Regulators found its solvency ratio had fallen below half the legally required minimum following adjustments to its financial statements. Ueno itself had grown rapidly since launching in 2021, becoming one of Paraguay’s most prominent digital lenders.

The bank claimed 3 million customers and managed around $850 million in public funds. Following the intervention, the bank temporarily restricted customer access to accounts and disrupted financial services. Authorities began arranging account transfers and deposit protection while investigators examined the bank’s operations.

The crisis also triggered political fallout. President Santiago Peña announced his resignation on November 5 following mounting pressure over Ueno’s collapse. Reuters reported that prosecutors were investigating him, while authorities issued arrest warrants for eight bank executives.

Meanwhile, the USDT premium attracted attention across cryptocurrency markets. A November 5 review by Criptoinforme examined 80 Binance P2P advertisements. It found that the median price across the 10 best offers for buying USDT stood near 6,399 guaraníes. This represented a 3.4% premium over exchange-house dollar prices.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

Paraguay’s banking problems carry an interesting historical connection to Bitcoin’s creation. Satoshi Nakamoto published the Bitcoin whitepaper on October 31, 2008, during the global financial crisis. It proposed a peer-to-peer electronic cash system that could transfer value without relying on financial institutions.

The message became even clearer when Nakamoto mined Bitcoin’s genesis block on January 3, 2009. Its embedded newspaper headline read: “Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks.”

Bitcoin was designed to address the limitations of a financial system built around trusted intermediaries. Its decentralized network allows users to hold and transfer BTC without requiring permission from a conventional bank.

Paraguay’s situation demonstrates why that proposition still matters. If a bank restricts access to customer accounts, financial independence becomes more than an abstract crypto talking point.

Bitcoin takes another approach through decentralized ownership and self-custody. Users who control their private keys can access their BTC without depending on a bank to authorize withdrawals.

Bitcoin’s original promise was never simply about making investors wealthier. It was about giving people another way to hold and transfer value without depending entirely on the banking system. Paraguay has provided a timely reminder of why that idea emerged in the first place.

The short-term outlook stays mildly bullish as long as the $1,150 support holds. A proper recovery above $1,300 would confirm that buyers are back. A drop below $1,100 could mean a deeper correction.

Cardano (ADA) just can't catch a break, it's trading near $0.1908 after a long slide from its October highs around $0.28. The daily chart keeps getting worse, with lower highs, lower lows, and repeated failures to get back above key moving averages.

After a short recovery in September and early October, ADA hit strong resistance between $0.25 and $0.28. The rejection brought the bears back and pushed ADA below several important technical indicators.

ADA is now trading below its short-, medium-, and long-term moving averages, which makes the bearish outlook even stronger. These averages are pointing down, so sellers are clearly in control.

The closest support is around $0.185–$0.190, where the price is trying to find a temporary floor. A confirmed break below $0.185 could send ADA to the $0.175 support, and then to the stronger $0.160–$0.165 demand zone.

Buyers need to reclaim $0.200 to show the first signs of recovery. Stronger resistance sits between $0.215 and $0.230, where several moving averages meet. A proper breakout above $0.230 would be a real improvement for the chart.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is getting close to oversold territory, which shows the downside momentum isn't fading. This can come before short-term relief rallies, but on its own it doesn't confirm a bullish reversal.

Trading volume is still fairly low, so buyers don't seem convinced even after the recent drop. The short-term outlook for ADA stays bearish as long as the price is below $0.215.

If buyers defend $0.185, ADA could bounce toward $0.2-$0.215. If this support breaks, ADA is more likely to drop further toward $0.175 and possibly $0.160.

Until ADA makes higher lows and reclaims its major moving averages, any move up looks more like a short bounce than a proper bullish reversal.

#5377. Rivian spinout Also was working on an e-moto project in Kenya — until it walked away

Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.

Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE.

Also, the micromobility startup spun out of Rivian in 2025, quietly started and then walked away from an electric two-wheeler pilot project in Kenya earlier this year, as it sought to focus its resources on its consumer e-bike and autonomous vehicle ambitions, TechCrunch has learned.

The project received grant funding from the Shell Foundation, an independent charity established by the British oil and gas giant Shell plc. A section of the Shell Foundation’s website that has since been removed said the project’s goal was to “enable and de-risk global OEM entry into Africa’s EV market by piloting a locally integrated electric two-wheeler platform in Kenya, with potential to scale across East Africa.”

According to the deleted section, Also was expected to work on modular battery designs and distributed EV charging, and planned on “developing a purpose-built electric motorcycle for African riders.”

The opportunity for electric motorcycles seems ripe on the continent, which has a massive two-wheeler market. African mobility company Spiro recently said it has more than 130,000 electric motorcycles operating across seven countries, along with 2,500 battery-swapping stations. This boom has drawn interest from Chinese mobility companies and investors, which are pouring resources into the space.

In a September email, Also told TechCrunch that it had “explored this project” with an unnamed partner, but ultimately “decided to focus on its core roadmap” after completing only “some early-stage work.” Also said the grant funding it received from the Shell Foundation “will follow the project to support its ongoing development,” but declined to offer specifics.

The Shell Foundation told TechCrunch in an email that the project was “intended to generate evidence on driver income uplift potential, operational performance and commercial viability to deepen the company’s understanding of the market opportunity.” But when TechCrunch asked for more specifics, the Shell Foundation declined, citing a nondisclosure agreement with Also. Days later, the project disappeared from the Shell Foundation’s website.

During an interview last month at TechCrunch Disrupt, Also co-founder and president Chris Yu said the Kenya pilot project initially made sense given Also’s mission to build small, purpose-built vehicles that are “first and foremost cost-optimized to do the job that needs to be done in a particular market.”

But other projects took precedence, Yu said, especially the development of small autonomous vehicles — which Also is working on as part of a partnership with DoorDash.

“We piloted and ultimately decided, largely because of just urgency and pace around autonomy, frankly, that our attention would be best, in the near term, served fully focused” on that, he said, adding that he thinks there’s a “high chance that autonomy will show up first, and at a broader scale in these types of purpose-built smaller vehicles than at scale in passenger vehicles.”

Also walked away from the Africa project during a somewhat rocky first year of independence.

Supply chain problems forced the company to repeatedly delay deliveries of its first product, a premium e-bike called the TM-B, frustrating customers who had reserved one. What made matters worse was Also’s relative silence. The company said little for much of 2026 about when the bikes would arrive — a communication failure its leadership now acknowledges was a mistake.

“I think we did a pretty poor job communicating to our reservation holders through the summer when they were all waiting, and we got called out for that,” Yu said in the interview. “But I think it’s actually great. It’s really hard to earn the opportunity for people to care, and to tell us what they think, and to help us improve.”

Getting its first product launch back on track is crucial for Also, which has ambitions far beyond e-bikes. The company plans to sell commercial cargo bikes to companies like Amazon, including four-wheeled models, and has the partnership with DoorDash. These products are next in the company’s pipeline, Yu said, and represent bigger revenue opportunities.

But the TM-B comes first. It’s Also’s most visible product to consumers, and its striking design has drawn plenty of curiosity.

Yu said no single problem was responsible for delaying the bikes, which finally started shipping to customers in early October. Instead, Also spent much of the year playing supply chain Whac-A-Mole, a particularly difficult challenge given the TM-B’s complexity. Yu described the bike as “kind of a computer on wheels.”

At one point, Also found itself competing for the same raw materials used to make printed circuit boards for AI data centers. At other times, the company struggled to navigate certification requirements with different government agencies.

Yu said the scope of these problems, and the pace at which new ones popped up — almost weekly — made it difficult to give customers reliable updates about why their bikes were delayed.

“The entire team is like running at a million miles an hour to get these things produced and shipped to customers, and then it’s also really dynamic as well,” he said. “I think what we could have done better is just [say], straight up: ‘We’re chasing down these things, we’ll have an update shortly.’”

That didn’t happen at first, but Also has steadily improved its communication, earning some goodwill from customers on Reddit. The company will need it as it works through the inevitable kinks that come with a first product. Early customers have already reported problems, including delivery damage and noticeable battery drain.

#5376. Hollywood Prediction Market Faces Insider Scare: James Bond Casting Bets Shift

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Hollywood studios are tightening restrictions on employees betting on prediction market after suspicious activity surrounding the next James Bond casting decision. The prediction market controversy intensified after a platform temporarily pulled its market following a sudden wave of bets backing Callum Turner.

The Hollywood Reporter reported that studios and production companies have been quietly warning employees against wagering on confidential industry information. The restrictions cover casting decisions, movie release dates, and studio earnings. At least one company has reportedly established an anonymous hotline for reporting suspected insider betting.

THR has learned studios and production companies have been quietly issuing new guidelines to employees warning them not to engage in prediction market betting.• The warnings prohibit employees from placing bets on news events like studio earnings, casting, or even release… pic.twitter.com/JbiovSwZC9

The crackdown follows growing interest in entertainment contracts on platforms such as Polymarket and Kalshi. Employees could potentially turn confidential production information into profits before announcements reach the public. They are also being warned against passing information to friends or relatives who could place bets on their behalf.

A prediction market platform temporarily suspended its next James Bond casting market after a sudden wave of sharp money pushed Callum Turner ahead of longtime favorite Jack Lowden. The movement raised concerns that traders might have received information about the casting decision before an official announcement.

Turner’s odds had already improved following casting rumors and reports of screen tests. However, the sudden betting activity attracted additional attention, particularly because Amazon MGM Studios has yet to announce its next 007.

Domer who has made over $2,000,000 trading prediction markets doesn't believe Callum Turner will be the next James Bond despite him being the current favorite“Now Callum Turner, he's at like 75 cents off some rumors or whatever”“Basically I'm betting on none of the current… pic.twitter.com/9cEJXr3yde

Kalshi’s November 6 market snapshot showed Turner leading with a 62% implied probability. Josh O’Connor followed at 18%, while Lowden held 14%. Prediction market has become an increasingly attractive target for traders seeking opportunities beyond politics and sports, such as Hollywood.

Entertainment contracts can cover award winners, reality television eliminations, celebrity appearances, and confidential production developments. The potential for insider betting is particularly concerning when employees have access to information that ordinary participants cannot obtain.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

The controversy also highlights the infrastructure demands facing blockchain applications as prediction markets expand into entertainment and other real-world events. Faster execution and affordable transactions could become increasingly important as developers explore new onchain financial products.

Bitcoin Layer 2 projects are pursuing similar infrastructure improvements. Bitcoin Hyper uses the Solana Virtual Machine (SVM) to support high-throughput execution, lower transaction costs, and programmable applications while periodically settling Layer 2 state to Bitcoin.

Too fast. Too strong. Too Hyper. 🔥⚡️https://t.co/VNG0P4GuDo pic.twitter.com/oLavMFuU7w

It currently records more than $33.2 million raised, with HYPER priced at just $0.0136. The project also offers 35% staking rewards, while its November 26 presale deadline approaches.

The development effort aims to extend Bitcoin beyond traditional transfers and long-term storage. Its proposed ecosystem includes decentralized finance, payments, and other applications that require faster transaction processing.

Hollywood restrictions show a difficult enforcement problem for prediction market platforms such as Polymarket and Kalshi. Blockchain transactions can provide publicly accessible records of wallet activity, but identifying the person controlling an address is another matter. Traders can also use multiple wallets and intermediaries to make their activity harder to connect to their real identities.

The issue is not entirely theoretical. Kalshi previously fined a video editor working for MrBeast’s company $20,000 after the employee reportedly generated approximately $5,000 through bets using confidential information. Beast Industries subsequently fired the employee.

Kalshi Sues Mr Beast Editor for insider trading on the beast game ‘They insider traded about $4k,was Mr beast aware of his editor making bet of his show’ ‘imagine people doing this with anime predicting the outcome of the anime whereas there is already a manga’A lot of… pic.twitter.com/yCyu4r0GiD

Federal prosecutors have also pursued separate prediction-market cases involving an active-duty soldier and a Google engineer. Both cases involve allegations of using confidential information to place bets.

Hollywood restricting employees from betting in prediction market is only the first step, and the next James Bond announcement may finally settle the casting speculation.

Fal, a San Francisco-based startup that hosts and runs AI video, image, and audio models, has raised $1.3 billion in its latest funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Nvidia, Sound Ventures, and T. Rowe Price. The deal values Fal at $16 billion, double its $8 billion valuation in April, Bloomberg reported.

The startup announced its Series E and F rounds at the same time, noting that a combined $1.65 billion was raised across both. (Sequoia led the earlier round.)

The latest round (Series F) comes amid soaring demand for inference services, the process of running an AI model that’s already been trained to generate outputs, particularly from customers relying on open source models. Fal surpassed $800 million in annualized revenue earlier this year, Bloomberg’s report noted.

Companies providing inference services, including Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Modal, have also been growing rapidly and raising large funding rounds at higher valuations. But their gross margins remain thin because of the high cost of buying or leasing compute, according to several people familiar with inference companies’ financials.

Fal was co-founded in 2021 by Burkay Gur, a former Coinbase machine learning leader and Oracle engineer, and Gorkem Yurtseven, who was previously a developer at Amazon.

#5374. Binance Hacker Continues Aggressive Bitcoin Buying Spree

The hacker behind the monumental Binance attack is still buying up more Bitcoin (BTC).

As per the latest blockchain analytics data from Lookonchain dated Nov. 4, the hacker continues to exchange SOL for Bitcoin, moving the stolen assets across several crypto wallets.

The blockchain tracker added that the hacker is using the following multi-step process to exchange the stolen crypto for Bitcoin.

The hacker’s complicated scheme involves splitting his SOL assets among different wallets before selling the SOL for USDC, transferring the USDC from Solana to Ethereum, buying ETH using the USDC and finally exchanging the newly bought ETH for BTC using THORChain, a decentralized cross-chain liquidity protocol.

This long and complicated cross-chain transaction process allows the hacker to easily transfer his funds between different blockchain networks. It also makes it harder to trace the stolen assets.

This in not the first time that the hacker has been buying Bitcoin with the stolen funds. In fact, he had earlier been seen making transactions to buy Bitcoin using tens of millions of dollars’ worth of stolen SOL.

As per Lookonchain’s data dated Nov. 1, the hacker behind the Binance hack was trying to convert approximately 970,522 SOL, worth roughly $95.9 million at the time of writing, into Bitcoin.

The hacker was even seen making a transaction involving 486,970 SOL (approximately $46.4M) in just one hour.

However, during these transactions, the hacker used a different service called Relay Protocol, which also allows cross-chain crypto transfers.

From the recent blockchain data, it looks like the hacker is still focused on Bitcoin. He’s also using several decentralized services to exchange the stolen crypto.

The latest official update from Binance shows that the massive security breach has affected crypto assets worth around $6.34 billion.

As per the update, the exchange says that it has frozen/intercepted about $2.85 billion worth of stolen cryptocurrency as of Nov. 3.

According to US federal authorities, the attack was conducted by a North Korean state-sponsored hacker group called TraderTraitor.

The FBI is also asking various decentralized crypto services like THORChain to prevent funds linked to the attack from moving around.

Even with all these efforts, the latest on-chain data shows that the hacker is still moving stolen funds across different networks.

The crypto market is in for another bumpy ride as financial events coincide with a spike in volatility, and around $435 million in positions have been liquidated over the past 24 hours. Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH) are taking the biggest hit, and leveraged traders keep losing money on major exchanges.

According to CoinGlass, total liquidations reached $440 million, hitting 91,821 traders. Shorts accounted for $171 million. Longs took the bigger hit with $269 million, or 61.2% of the total, which shows that most of the pain fell on traders betting on a rise.

Bitcoin led with $163.8 million in liquidations, followed by Ethereum at $68 million. Other coins added $50 million in total liquidations, which makes the distribution of liquidations somewhat equal here.

Bitcoin's daily chart looks somewhat fragile as BTC is trading around $78,006 after a pullback from its October highs near $87,000, which is an unfortunate sign, suggesting the recovery continuation is unlikely here.

BTC is now testing a key support zone between $76,000 and $78,000, where the longer-term moving averages collide. In a case where resistance is broken, new support should arise around $74,000 and possibly $70,000.

The closest resistance is near $80,000-$82,000, with multiple moving averages forming a trend, which will act as a resistance with Bitcoin's ascending movement.

Momentum indicators prompt further weakness, with the Relative Strength Index (RSI) slipping towards the lower half of its range. Bullish momentum is fading, but the market isn't extremely oversold yet.

Hyperliquid saw around $39.84 million in liquidations over four hours, or 40.8% of the total for that period. Binance came next with $29 million, and OKX recorded $9.09 million.

The largest single liquidation reported was $5.03 million on Binance's ETHUSDT market.

The liquidation numbers don't prove that the outside events caused the sell-off. Traders cutting risks and high leverage could make the swings even bigger. If Bitcoin holds the $76,000 support zone, the market might calm down, but unfortunately, there's another big wave of liquidations sitting just around the corner in case of a breakdown.

The current decline in XRP's market value has not led to loss-taking by large stakeholders — on the contrary, a phase of aggressive accumulation has unfolded in the market. According to data from the analytical platform Santiment, an absolute record for the current year has been set on the XRP Ledger network: 2,147 wallets now hold a balance of 1 million tokens or more.

The main inflow of capital came during the price correction period, when the asset's market price dropped to the $1.27 mark.

The main activity of large capital unfolded at the end of October. The dynamics with which investors are forming large positions points to a rigid strategic calculation: over the past ten days, 28 new addresses have attained millionaire status, and 18 of them were opened during the final three days of the reporting period.

Unlike speculative capital oriented toward quick profit, large holders traditionally use phases of price weakness for buying. The growth in the number of millionaires at such a moment confirms that large balances are being systematically increased rather than liquidated.

Such divergences between a falling chart and an inflow of institutional capital often precede the formation of a long-term market bottom.

Is this surge a signal that the price has found a bottom? Analysts identify three clear price thresholds that will give a precise answer to this question in the coming days:

• The $1.20 – $1.25 zone (Foundation): A critical support line and the main indicator of a potential bottom. If the price holds in this range and the number of millionaire wallets remains above 2,140, the long-term growth scenario will remain in force.

• The $1.30 milestone (Psychology): A local resistance level, a return above which is necessary to confirm a reversal and restore optimism in the mass market.

• The $1.40 level (Confirmation): Consolidation of the price above this mark amid a continuing inflow of large holders will prove that the bottom has been definitively passed and that capital is ready to drive the asset toward new highs.

Thus, the sustainability of XRP's current bullish setup depends directly on the ability of large capital to hold key support levels during the coming market movements.

#5368. Solana Co-Founder Names Biggest Threat to Crypto

Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko said phishing and social engineering attacks are the biggest threat to crypto and advised investors to worry more about social engineering attacks than about AI or quantum computers breaking crypto security.

"Phishing and social engineering is the biggest threat to crypto. Not AI breaking math or quantum computers," he wrote on X.

The Solana co-founder also suggested having a separate iOS device with Apple's Lockdown Mode turned on and using a multisignature crypto wallet.

This is one of the cheapest ways for investors to safeguard their digital assets, according to Yakovenko.

The Solana co-founder's statement highlights a fundamental weakness in crypto security: hackers don't need to break blockchain security to steal digital assets.

What they can do is fool crypto holders into giving them access to their assets.

Phishing involves using malicious emails, sites or messages to trick people into revealing sensitive information such as crypto wallet recovery phrases, account information, etc.

Social engineering is a broader term that describes attacks in which hackers manipulate victims into doing something that can compromise their security.

Yakovenko's point becomes crystal clear with the recent massive hack at Binance.

The world's largest crypto exchange, Binance, faced a security breach on Oct. 29 that affected around $6.34 billion in digital assets.

According to Binance's Nov. 3 investigation update, the hackers carried out a sophisticated social engineering attack, which included fake job interviews to compromise Binance employees.

A Binance software engineer was targeted by people pretending to be representatives of a fake company. The Binance employee went through some fake job interviews. The employee was convinced to download what seemed to be a legitimate technical assignment.

But the downloaded file contained malicious code that helped the hackers compromise the employee's computer.

Then, the hackers used the compromised devices, stolen credentials and an internal AI tool to access Binance's wallet infrastructure.

Eventually, this helped the hackers execute unauthorized crypto transfers from the exchange's hot wallets.

The Security Alliance (SEAL) released a report on Nov. 4 stating that its security team handled 99 incidents from Oct. 28 to Nov. 3.

In three of those incidents involving fraudulent customer support calls, victims lost roughly $1.57 million and 1.12 BTC from Oct. 28 to Nov. 3.

One of the scams involved fake Apple support representatives stealing a victim's Apple ID credentials. The victim had saved their crypto recovery phrase in cloud storage. Another victim shared their wallet recovery phrase during a fake Telegram support call.

The group also tracked 5,137 phishing domains during this reporting period.

#5366. Can You Put Crypto Mining in Space? Elon Musk's Data Center Idea Can Be Used in Crypto

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Elon Musk did what he does best on X: fresh speculations via post on November 4, saying: “Data centers in space look pretty appealing right now.”

Musk was talking about data centers, but the idea can be used in crypto too: could Bitcoin mining rigs work in orbit, powered only by the Sun? Technically, they should, why not? Economically, however, it's getting a bit more complicated.

Space has one big advantage: plenty of solar energy. Unlike mining farms on Earth, orbital mining stations could use large solar ray to make their own electricity without any power grid. Satellites today could get constant powering from sunlight, leading to a lower battery consumption.

Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now

In theory, Bitcoin ASIC miners could then run around the clock with very low or non-existent ongoing electricity costs. The problem is that solar panels, batteries, power electronics and would all have to be launched into orbit–that's the part where problems arise.

Space might look like the perfect place to cool mining equipment, since the cosmic background is extremely cold. Unfortunately, it's not so simple and the vacuum in space actually makes cooling harder than on earth.

Here, mining rigs get rid of heat with fans, air conditioning or liquid cooling, in orbit, there's no air at all that will be able to push the air away. So the only option out there seems to be the liquid cooling, large radiator panels which should be able to release heat as infrared radiation.

According to Boston Consulting Group (BCG), a 100-kilowatt orbital data center could need around a whopping 400 square meters of radiators. But apart from technical challenges, we should always keep in mind the profitability. Getting equipment to space in the first place is what makes the whole idea questionable.

According to BCG, launching to orbit currently costs around $1,500 per kilogram. That means, a one-ton mining setup would cost around $1.5 million just to launch, excluding hardware, cooling, solar arrays and maintenance that will cost just as much if not more.

You also can't ignore space radiation, equipment failures and limited chances for repairs that add even more costs at the top of it. The only thing that can somehow make math look better is more efficient ASIC chips and ways of delivering goods to space at the fraction of today's costs.

Thankfully, Bitcoin miners need little to no bandwidth, so the connection issue is somewhat solved on its own.

Physically, mining Bitcoin in space is possible: is it justifiable financially though? Not really. Reusable rockets, lightweight cooling and other things might make it more financially viable, but as of today, we should be sticking with good old mining rigs in huge hangars on Earth.

#5365. A YC startup is putting $1M behind 5 unsolved materials science problems for AI

Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.

Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE.

Discovered Materials, a months-old San Francisco startup using AI models to find new substances for building advanced chips, announced a million-dollar challenge for AI models to solve five critical problems in materials science.

While frontier AI models have solved a remarkable series of outstanding mathematics problems and made progress in the life sciences, they have yet to truly plumb the complex physics in advanced materials.

“It’s more difficult to specify problems clearly in materials science because it’s not like math, where you have a very specific definition and can get to a yes or no,” said Advaith Sridhar, a co-founder of Discovered Materials, which was part of Y Combinator’s spring 2026 batch. “We came to this discussion [wondering], what are the grand challenges in this field? How do we know AI is making progress?”

Though materials science doesn’t have an equivalent of the Millennium Prize Problems, Discovered Materials recruited an advisory group of academics at leading global universities to spell out five open problems. The company is offering a pool of prizes, worth $1 million in total, for solutions to the problems.

“Across materials science, there are phenomena we observe but cannot explain,” Felipe Jornada, a Stanford professor who helped develop the challenges, said in a statement. “Explaining these phenomena would improve our understanding of physics, and the answers would directly shape how we build electronics, store energy, and manufacture the materials of the future.”

Before announcing the challenges, Discovered Materials turned frontier lab models loose on them, giving AI agents internet access and other resources to work autonomously for days. The models spent several days on each problem without making much headway. Still, it’s easy to imagine OpenAI or Anthropic attempting to one-shot them with significantly more compute or a newer model.

“It’s not particularly a concern to us whether we find it, or someone else finds it, or a professor finds it, or the frontier labs find it,” Sridhar said. “The reason we’re putting out these challenges is because we want them to serve as the goalposts. If you go and solve these challenges, we are deepening our understanding of materials and how things around us behave.”

Tracking efforts to solve the problems will show “whether the models are climbing in this domain,” he added.

The challenge also reflects the changing nature of scientific inquiry as AI proves capable of uncovering insights and techniques human researchers didn’t anticipate. With solutions apparently easier to find than ever, the questions become more important.

“This is a new way of thinking about science, where we come up with the verification and the challenges first, and then we let somebody come up with the ideas that explain the problem,” Sridhar said. “Knowing what are the right questions to ask is not trivial and very difficult in this domain, so this is where the professors have really helped us shape what are the right questions we should be asking.”

Discovered Materials’ main focus is developing new materials for use in semiconductors; the startup partners with chip giants on research projects while also funding its own scientific efforts. When the company announced its seed round in August, Sridhar told TechCrunch that he hoped the company would generate a useful material within a year.

“Those timelines have accelerated a little bit,” he says today. “I’m more confident now that we will be able to find these industrially useful materials in a timeline shorter than a year.”

#5364. Dogecoin Contributor Shares Key Safety Reminder Amid Binance Withdrawal Resumption

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Dogecoin community member Mishaboar has shared a fresh safety reminder to DOGE holders as cryptocurrency withdrawals resume on Binance following the exchange's recent security incident.

Binance began restoring withdrawals in phases on November 1, 2026, with that of Dogecoin already restored. Binance has also published a cryptographic Proof of Reserves for selected assets, including Dogecoin, based on its October 31 snapshot.

A few updates on the Binance situation since my last post. - The Hack Binance has finally published its initial technical findings, and, as we had expected, the attack was considerably more complicated than the original explanation involving a compromised devops laptop. According to Binance, the attackers targeted multiple engineers through malicious software, including an earlier attempt involving a tampered devtool installer and a fake job interview that delivered malware. They then exploited an internal AI tool and stolen deployment credentials to gain access to Binance's wallet-signing infrastructure. On Ethereum, malicious EIP-7702 authorizations allowed the attackers to continue moving funds even after Binance had suspended normal withdrawals. It's difficult to understand why the signing controls allowed these authorizations in the first place. I am curious to know how it is possible the authorizations were not detected more quickly, and why revoking them took so long on wallets holding such gigantic amounts. Binance says it took almost four hours to fully contain the attack. It will be good to see independent reviews from competent security analysts. - Withdrawals/Deposits (after withdrawals reopened) According to figures shared by Binance co-CEO Richard Teng and reported by CoinDesk, approximately $10.97 billion was withdrawn during the first 46 hours after withdrawals reopened, against $5.69 billion in deposits. That leaves approximately $5.28 billion in net outflows, as of early November 3. Withdrawal activity was particularly intense on Sunday, but appears to have slowed down since. Binance claims that hourly deposits had started exceeding withdrawals by the end of that period. - The Money Binance reported approximately $2.85 billion frozen or intercepted in its November 3 update. Once again, remember that frozen funds are NOT necessarily recovered funds. Binance also says it has replaced the vast majority of affected assets using its own resources, including SAFU and insurance funds (see my previous update for considerations about this). The published replenishment percentages have been somewhat inconsistent, however. And once again, replacing stolen assets is NOT the same as recovering them from the attackers. Using SAFU and the Futures Insurance Fund to cover these losses also means that the risk profile of holding funds on the exchange may have shifted considerably. As exchanges operate largely within black boxes, it is difficult to assess this at this point. - Withdrawals and Proof of Reserves Binance has published a cryptographic Proof of Reserves for ten selected assets (including Dogecoin), based on its October 31 snapshot. That is considerably fewer than the 55 assets covered in its previous snapshot, with many smaller assets still missing. Once again, this is useful, but as I have explained multiple times, Proof of Reserves are never a comprehensive audit of an exchange's financial condition and stability. More cryptocurrency withdrawals are being restored in phases, although availability still depends on the specific asset and network. Native Dogecoin withdrawals were included in the first reopening phase. The usual reminder: please make sure you select the actual Dogecoin network when withdrawing to your own wallet, rather than stuff like Binance-pegged DOGE on BSC. My recommendation stays the same: withdraw when and if you can, without rushing, and after verifying that you have good backups of your wallets and that the wallet you are using is safe.

As native Dogecoin withdrawals have now been restored, Mishaboar shared his "usual reminder" to the Dogecoin community, telling them to ensure they select the actual Dogecoin network when withdrawing to their wallets, "rather than stuff like Binance-pegged DOGE on BSC," he said.

A Binance-Pegged Dogecoin, a BEP-20 token, runs on the BNB Smart Chain (BSC), and the distinction between it and the actual DOGE coin on the Dogecoin network remains essential to prevent confusion.

Mishaboar also advised users not to rush the withdrawal process, noting that wallet security and proper backup procedures should come first: "My recommendation remains the same: withdraw when and if you can, without rushing, and after verifying that you have good backups of your wallets and that the wallet you are using is secure."

Major crypto exchange Binance recently published initial findings and a response update on the October 29 security incident.

According to Binance, the attackers targeted multiple engineers through malicious software, including an earlier attempt involving a tampered devtool installer and a fake job interview that delivered malware. They then exploited an internal AI tool and stolen deployment credentials to gain access to Binance's wallet-signing infrastructure.

The incident involves assets of some $6.34 billion. About $2.85 billion worth of assets have been intercepted or frozen as of the update.

As of Oct. 31, 2026, Binance said it has restored 98% of the affected token assets and is working on purchasing outstanding, more illiquid assets.

Binance stated that the entry points identified as having been used in the attack have been closed, and it is engaging independent third-party cybersecurity experts to conduct a comprehensive review of the incident.

#5363. Aina’s smart ring has a screen, a joystick, and a mic so you can talk to AI agents

Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.

Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE.

Hardware startup Aina released a smart ring today that features a screen, a joystick, and a mic so that you can talk to your agents and take notes. The $399 ring has a speaker so you can take calls using it as well.

The startup, which raised $5.5 million in July, is positioning the ring as a controller of sorts for both AI and non-AI apps.

The company previously made Mirage, a three-key controller that let you invoke buttons based on the app on your Mac’s screen. For instance, if you were on a Google Meet call, you could map keys to camera on/off, mic mute/unmute, or to leave the meeting.

Aina has baked in lessons from that device to create the new ring, which it’s simply calling “AI ring.” Using its mic, you can take notes, send a prompt to agents, set reminders, and dictate notes on your Mac using Wispr Flow or the startup’s own dictation engine.

Now, there are already smart rings in the market that do similar things, like the Pebble Index 01, Sandbar Stream, Oasis, and Natura, which is probably why Aina has added more controls and functionality to stand out. Its ring comes with a speaker so that you can take calls, and there is a screen, which lets you see notifications from your phone or which apps you are controlling.

For navigation, there is a joystick, and it also supports gestures, so that it can trigger different actions based on what’s on your Mac or phone’s screen. The ring also lets you control music or even smart home devices like Apple TV.

I have used the ring for a few days, and it feels like a smartwatch in a ring format, with more controls. I can get notifications and reply to them. It surfaces my meetings; I can call Uber if I want to get a ride home.

It’s easier to use Apple TV’s remote itself, but the Aina ring proved useful the couple times I couldn’t find the remote. Granted, a lot of the software and features are still being fleshed out, so it’s hard to figure out where such a device ring might sit in my daily usage, but it is squarely aimed at folks who are surrounded by digital devices and AI applications.

“Phones and laptop screens were designed for an age of browsing where you think about opening apps. For interacting with proactive agents, we need a better interface, and that is what we had in mind while designing Aina,” Apoorv Shankar, Aina’s founder, told TechCrunch over a call.

Companies are trying to cater to programmers and AI enthusiasts with specialized hardware that could help them harness different agents. This includes OpenAI’s experimental keyboard and Rabbit trying to position itself as a controller. The hope with such hardware is that enough people will have multiple agents running to invest in specific gadgets to keep tabs on them.

Aina’s ring goes on preorder starting Thursday at early-bird pricing of $399, and the company plans to start shipping the device in January 2027. Once the early-bird period ends, the ring will cost $499.

Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.

Zipline has raised $1.5 billion and ramped up its partnership with Walmart, a pair of deals that have raised the autonomous drone delivery and logistics startup’s profile and valuation.

Zipline and Walmart reached a new multi-year agreement to add 300 drone delivery sites across the United States. The two companies have had a drone delivery agreement since 2021, but this deal is a significant jump from the 21 active drone delivery sites they have together today.

On the fundraising side, Zipline’s $1.5 billion raise was led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, with participation from Valor Equity Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Uber, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan, ARK Invest, and Salesforce Ventures. Zipline is now valued at $21.5 billion.

The company, which has developed a drone delivery ecosystem that includes aircraft, launch and landing systems, and logistics software, said it plans to use the funds to expand its U.S. manufacturing facilities and hire more workers to build out a nationwide drone delivery network.

Founded in 2014, Zipline got its start in Africa, where it used its autonomous drones to deliver blood in Rwanda, and later expanded to Ghana and Nigeria. The California-based company began its first operations in the U.S. in 2020, ferrying medical equipment and supplies to Novant Health in North Carolina. The following year, it struck a deal with Walmart.

But it was in 2022 that Zipline’s business really started to take off in the United States. Zipline received its Part 135 air carrier certification from the Federal Aviation Administration that year, a critical regulatory hurdle that authorized the company to complete long-range commercial drone deliveries. It has locked in a number of partnerships since then, including with Uber earlier this year.

Zipline now uses its drones to deliver food, retail, agricultural, and health products in five African countries, several cities in the United States, and Japan. Zipline’s home delivery service uses Zipline’s Platform 2 drones, which are designed to carry up to eight pounds and travel to customers within a 10-mile radius. Its larger Platform 1 drones are used for long-range deliveries for enterprise, business, and government that can cover 120 miles round trip.

The company said Thursday that its share of delivery revenue grew from 10.8% to 34.9% between March and October of this year. This latest funding aims to push that metric even higher.

Asian markets wiped out more than $1 trillion as technology stocks faced heavy selling pressure.

Japan’s Nikkei entered bear market territory after plunging 6% during Friday’s trading session.

Bitcoin fell toward $76,000 as strong US jobless data triggered nearly $1 billion in liquidations.

Asian stock markets are deepening their sell-off, with more than $1 trillion in market value wiped out today, after losing over $550 billion yesterday. Japan, South Korea, China and Taiwan all faced heavy losses, while Wall Street suffered a $2.5 trillion wipeout.

The crypto market did not escape the fallout, Bitcoin dropped below $76,000.

The Asian stock market sell-off intensified on 6 November as investors dumped technology and AI stocks over fears of US regulatory changes and a slowdown in AI infrastructure spending.

Japan suffered one of the biggest blows, with the Nikkei 225 dropping 6% and entering a bear market. The decline pushed Japan’s losses from its June record to 21%, wiping out roughly $450 billion in value.

South Korea followed with an even sharper move. The KOSPI collapsed 9% to 4,912, triggering a trading halt. The index is now around 47% below its June record, while SK Hynix fell 12% and Samsung Electronics dropped nearly 10%. South Korea has lost close to $203 billion.

China and Taiwan also joined the sell-off. Shenzhen has fallen 30% from its June high, erasing roughly $210 billion. The Shanghai Composite fell 1.1%, while the CSI 300 dropped 1.5%. In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng fell 1%, while its AI index plunged 4%.

Meanwhile, Taiwan’s TAIEX dropped 3.2% over 24 hours and is now 24% below its October record.

The weakness across Asia followed Wall Street’s worst single-session decline in more than a year. The S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73, while the Nasdaq dropped 6.52% to 24,315, entering correction territory after falling more than 10% from its October peak. The Dow dropped 3.44%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 10%, while Nvidia, Broadcom, Oracle, CoreWeave and Nebius also suffered heavy losses as investors pulled back from technology stocks.

Bitcoin also followed the broader market decline, falling from above $80,800 to around $75,500 to 76,000. A major trigger was the latest US Initial Jobless Claims report.

Claims unexpectedly fell to 189,000, below the 197,000 forecast and near levels last seen in 1969. While the data signaled a strong US economy, it reduced expectations for easier monetary policy, pressuring Bitcoin and other risk assets.

The sudden price move triggered roughly $1 billion in crypto liquidations, with 88% involving leveraged long positions.

Crypto stocks also suffered, with Coinbase and MicroStrategy falling roughly 10% to 11%.

#5358. 'Don’t Be Silly': Satoshi Associate Dismisses Bitcoin Quantum Collapse Claims

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Bitcoin developers have renewed the discussion about the long-term security of the network amid the development of quantum computing ("Q-Day"). The trigger was an interview StarkWare CEO Eli Ben-Sasson gave to journalist Pete Rizzo.

According to Ben-Sasson, without the implementation of a "quantum fix," Bitcoin will lose its leadership, and its market value will collapse due to the physical limitations of current computing systems.

Criticism of these forecasts came from Adam Back, the creator of Hashcash, co-founder of Blockstream and one of the cryptographers mentioned by Satoshi Nakamoto in the Bitcoin whitepaper. On the social network X, Back described the panic expectations with the phrase: "c'mon guys, don't be silly and alarmist."

According to Back, the risks are exaggerated, since algorithms for protection against quantum threats are already at the protocol planning stage. He pointed out that Ben-Sasson's own company, StarkWare, builds its products on STARK technology: zero-knowledge proofs that run on cryptographic hash functions.

In the Bitcoin technical community, hash functions are considered the main security factor. According to theoretical models, quantum computers running Shor's algorithm are capable of breaking the network's current asymmetric cryptography (ECDSA and Schnorr).

However, this method is ineffective against hash functions (including SHA-256). Grover's algorithm gives quantum systems only a quadratic speedup in brute-force search, which, according to Back, is fully neutralized by Bitcoin's standard security settings.

As an alternative scenario, Satoshi Nakamoto's associate cited data on the community's current technical developments, which by late 2026 have moved into the testing phase:

SHRINCS protocol: A modified hash-based signature (Shrunken SPHINCS). According to Blockstream developers, they optimized it for Bitcoin's bandwidth limits.

Implementation status: An official draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) has been published for review. According to the project's roadmap, the technology is undergoing stress tests on the Liquid sidechain.

Critics of post-quantum cryptography often name data volume as the main problem. Quantum-resistant signatures are bulkier than standard 64-byte Schnorr keys, which, according to a number of researchers, could overload the blockchain and raise fees.

Back argues that the infrastructure is capable of scaling through data aggregation. According to his position, batch verification methods and STARK hash proofs make it possible to compress thousands of signatures into one compact package. According to supporters of this approach, the solution will preserve the network's speed and protect its decentralization.

The current discussion demonstrates the existence of two polar views: part of the industry considers the quantum threat an urgent problem, while Bitcoin core developers speak of planned testing of the protective infrastructure, which is proceeding in parallel with the development of quantum capabilities.

A new blockchain project, Yellow, that previously attracted $10 million in personal investment from Ripple co-founder Chris Larsen has faced massive criticism from members of the XRP community immediately after the listing of its token. Observers’ attention was drawn to asset-selling operations from a wallet that is linked to the developers.

The project’s token was launched simultaneously on the Ethereum and XRP Ledger (XRPL) networks. Due to the absence of a direct technical bridge between the blockchains and high initial demand, the asset’s price on XRPL turned out to be significantly higher than on the Ethereum network.

During this period, tokens worth about 20,000 XRP were sold on the XRPL market from a wallet associated with the startup’s team. Project representative Burak Cem explained in private chats that these transactions were “team wallet arbitraging,” necessary to reduce the emerging price premium and align the rates.

The team’s actions provoked a mixed reaction in the community. Kaj Leroy, a developer popular in the XRP Ledger ecosystem, expressed doubt about the technical possibility of conducting full-fledged arbitrage trades without a working cross-chain bridge.

According to critics, such operations on the first day of trading effectively amount to “liquidity extraction” at the expense of early retail buyers.

The incident developed in the context of a public discussion started by influencer JC Rivera , who reproached the XRP community for systematic skepticism toward new startups. In response, opponents led by Kaj Leroy justified the community’s wariness with the new project’s on-chain data.

@JcRivera @xrplto because they dumped 20k xrp worth on their holders like instantly and said its for arbitrage?🤣 onboarding people to extract this obviously is not the way bro

In their opinion, external teams often use rhetoric about “onboarding” users, while their actions lead to locking in quick profits at the expense of XRP holders’ liquidity.

At the moment, the project, which plans to launch clearing solutions for AI agents, has not provided any additional official comments on the situation. The local community’s level of trust in the new startup remains under pressure.

Reece Merrick, Ripple Senior Executive Officer/Managing Director, Middle East & Africa, attended the recently concluded Dubai Fintech Summit held between November 2 and 3, 2026, organized by DIFC as part of Dubai Future Finance Week.

In 2024, Ripple announced a partnership with the DIFC Innovation Hub, the thriving innovation ecosystem of the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC), to accelerate blockchain innovation in the UAE.

Ripple announced in 2026 its expansion in the UAE with the opening of its Middle East and Africa (MEA) regional headquarters in the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC). The announcement highlighted the firm's strategic presence in the country.

Fantastic panel at @DubaiFinTechSum diving into how digital assets scale from here. The consensus was clear: the question is no longer if institutional adoption happens, but what infrastructure needs to change to support it. A few takeaways from our discussion with @BlackRock, @StanChart & @RobinhoodCrypto ➡️ The 24/7 reality: The next generation requires always-on rails. Markets with "opening hours" simply won't cut it. ➡️ Bridging TradFi & DeFi: Scaling tokenized markets requires real bank-grade infrastructure, custody, and risk management. At @Ripple, we see every day how enterprise rails, tokenization, and stablecoins bridge this gap 🇦🇪

In a recent X post, Merrick highlighted his participation at the Dubai Fintech Summit as part of a panel that explored how digital assets could scale. The details gathered from his X post revealed that representatives from BlackRock, Standard Chartered and Robinhood were also participants in this discussion.

Merrick said the consensus among participants was clear, as the question was no longer whether institutional adoption would happen, but what infrastructure needed to change to support it.

The Ripple executive went on to share a few takeaways from the discussion with BlackRock, Standard Chartered and Robinhood executives in his X post.

First was the growing need for financial infrastructure that operates around the clock. Merrick noted that the next generation of digital asset markets will require always-on payment and settlement systems, rather than relying on traditional market opening hours. "The 24/7 reality: The next generation requires always-on rails. Markets with 'opening hours' just won't cut it," Merrick wrote.

The second point was about the importance of bridging traditional finance (TradFi) and decentralized finance (DeFi). Merrick said that to achieve growth in tokenized markets, institutions will need bank-grade infrastructure, reliable custody solutions and effective risk management systems to participate at scale.

"Bridging TradFi & DeFi: Scaling tokenized markets requires real bank-grade infrastructure, custody, and risk management," Merrick wrote.

Elizabeth Warren could become Senate Banking Committee chairwoman after Democrats take control in January 2027.

Warren would gain subpoena powers, giving her greater authority to investigate crypto companies.

The CLARITY Act could face another major challenge under Warren’s expected committee leadership.

Crypto Critic Elizabeth Warren is expected to become the chairwoman of the Senate Banking Committee in January 2027. That could give her new powers to investigate crypto companies, demand documents, and question industry leaders.

But who could face her first, and what could this mean for the CLARITY Act?

When the new Congress begins on January 3, 2027, Elizabeth Warren is in line to become chairwoman of the Senate Banking Committee. This is because Senate committee leadership usually follows seniority rules.

Former Democratic leader Senator Sherrod Brown has announced his retirement at the end of his term in 2025, leaving the top Democratic position on the committee open.

Her appointment is not formally final, but few observers expect a serious challenge.

The role would give Warren much more power over financial markets and the crypto industry. As a senator, she has largely relied on letters and requests for information from crypto companies. As chairwoman, she would gain subpoena power, allowing the committee to formally demand documents and testimony.

This could lead to stricter checks on major crypto companies and their leaders.

One of Warren’s first priorities could be putting crypto companies under closer scrutiny. She has already questioned regulators about giving crypto firms bank-like approvals.

Coinbase, Ripple, and Trump-linked World Liberty Financial are among the companies she has raised concerns about. As chair, she could ask for more details and hold public hearings.

Warren is also looking beyond crypto companies. In October, she and Republican Senator John Curtis questioned Kalshi and Polymarket over possible insider trading and market manipulation in election-related markets.

Her third major target could be Trump-linked crypto businesses. Warren has repeatedly questioned the relationship between President Donald Trump, his family, and digital asset ventures. She previously asked the SEC to investigate whether World Liberty Financial misled investors.

The first major battle could be the CLARITY Act. The bill failed to advance in the Senate after a 49-50 vote in September, falling short of the 60 votes needed to move forward.

The bill already failed to clear a key Senate vote in September. If lawmakers cannot pass it before January 3, a Democratic-controlled Senate could make another attempt much harder.

As committee chair, Warren could influence which financial bills move forward, potentially slowing industry-friendly crypto legislation and keeping companies under greater regulatory pressure.

The political shift comes while Bitcoin is already under pressure. Bitcoin is already trading below $76,000, nearly 40% below its roughly $126,000 all-time high, as the market faces pressure from the recent US technology sell-off and broader economic concerns

A Warren-led Banking Committee could add another source of uncertainty, especially if tougher investigations and stricter crypto oversight become a priority in 2027.

#5344. Bitcoin, Ether ETFs draw $128M as crypto rebounds after midterms

Fidelity led Bitcoin ETF inflows, while BlackRock’s IBIT shed another $201 million, extending its outflow streak to four trading sessions.

US-listed spot Bitcoin and Ether exchange-traded funds (ETFs) snapped their outflow streaks on Wednesday as cryptocurrency markets rebounded following the US midterm elections.

Bitcoin (BTC) ETFs attracted $74.6 million on Wednesday, while Ether (ETH) funds added $53 million, according to SoSoValue data.

The turnaround ended three consecutive trading sessions of Bitcoin ETF outflows totaling $1.16 billion, while Ether ETFs snapped a seven-day outflow streak of $657 million.

Bitcoin rebounded above $80,000 and US stocks rallied following Democrats’ midterm election victories on Wednesday.

The latest batch of inflows followed a slowdown in withdrawals, from $399 million on Monday to $116 million on Tuesday.

Blackrock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded another $201.2 million in outflows on Wednesday, extending its four-session outflow streak to $935.2 million, according to Farside Investors data. Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC), meanwhile, led inflows with roughly $237 million.

Daily spot Bitcoin ETF flows by issuer since Oct. 30. Source: Farside Investors

Wednesday’s inflows narrowed Bitcoin’s 2026 net outflows to around $79 million.

James Butterfill, head of research at digital asset manager CoinShares, said Bitcoin had largely priced in the possibility of a Democratic sweep before the election, leaving room for a relief rally as uncertainty eased. He cautioned against attributing too much of Bitcoin’s performance to the election outcome.

CK Zheng, co-founder of crypto hedge fund ZX Squared Capital and former global head of risk at Credit Suisse, pointed to monetary liquidity, institutional investment flows and broader investor appetite for risk as more immediate drivers of Bitcoin’s price.

Related: Trump-linked tokens lead crypto losses after Democrats sweep in the US midterms

Zheng said spot Bitcoin ETFs and corporate treasury holdings could broaden demand while also exposing BTC to institutional selling pressure.

World Liberty Financial launched a long-term buyback program for its struggling WLFI governance token.

The buyback may use revenue from USD1 stablecoin reserve fees and other ecosystem sources.

Meanwhile, WLFI token remains down more than 73%, highlighting the scale of its post-election decline.

World Liberty Financial (WLF), the cryptocurrency venture backed by the Trump family, has launched a formal token buyback program for its WLFI governance token. The move comes as WLFI remains down more than 73% since its post-election drop.

Here are the details of the buyback plan.

On November 6, World Liberty Financial announced a new buyback program for its WLFI governance token. The company plans to use revenue from its ecosystem, including fees earned from reserves backing its USD1 stablecoin, to buy back WLFI tokens.

However, WLFI has not revealed how much money it will spend or when the purchases will begin.

The plan is designed to do more than reduce WLFI’s circulating supply.

“The goal is to encourage active participation in WLFI governance and consolidate voting power among our most committed long-term holders.”

Importantly, the company described the buyback as a long-term plan, not a one-time move. This matters because only around 32% of WLFI’s 100 billion token supply is currently circulating.

The Trump family also owns about 38% of the company behind the project, with its crypto interests including WLFI and the USD1 stablecoin.

The success of $USD1 and the growing WLFI ecosystem is helping us launch a new $WLFI token buyback program to strengthen the WLFI ecosystem and governance.We plan to fund buybacks with an initial allocation that may include fees earned from USD1 reserves and other sources.…

The timing of the announcement comes after a major sell-off in Trump-linked tokens following the 2026 US midterm elections, where Democrats made major gains.

WLFI plunged roughly 10% immediately after election night, adding to an already weak year for the token. From its November 2025 high of $0.1744, WLFI has fallen more than 73% to now trading near $0.047.

The pressure is not limited to WLFI. The Official Trump (TRUMP) token has fallen roughly 85% over the past year, while Melania Meme (MELANIA) has dropped around 41% this year.

The buyback also comes as Democrats prepare to take control of key congressional committees in January.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, expected to become chairwoman of the Senate Banking Committee, has already criticized Trump-linked crypto businesses and could push investigations into the Trump family’s DeFi operations, overseas capital links, and banking efforts.

#5340. Circle's USDC Dominates Stablecoin Market With 79% Share of Transaction Volume

Circle revealed that USDC accounted for 79% of the transaction volume of all stablecoins in the third quarter of 2026.

According to CEO Jeremy Allaire, the CEO of Circle explained that USDC's market share of the transaction volume of all stablecoins increased significantly from 66% in the same period a year ago. The overall USDC on-chain transaction volume was $13.9 trillion, an increase of 49% year-on-year.

This shows the rapid adoption of USDC in payments, trading, and blockchain-based financial applications despite stiff competition in the stablecoin space.

Circle stated that the issuance and redemption volumes of USDC in the third quarter reached a new high. In total, $208 billion of USDC was issued and redeemed in Q3. This translates to an average daily amount of $2.3 billion. For the third quarter, Circle said that the average USDC in circulation was $73.3 billion, which was up 18% year-on-year. This information was part of Circle's Q3 highlights.

Apart from USDC itself, Circle emphasized the growth in other aspects of its infrastructure. Circle indicated that Arc Mainnet went live in the third quarter. Over 100 institutions and applications are already building on Arc. As of Oct. 30, 2026, assets on Arc totaled $1.5 billion, as stated by Circle.

Circle Payment Network, or CPN, was another part of Circle's infrastructure that witnessed rapid growth. The company indicated that CPN ended the third quarter with an annualized payment volume of $41.3 billion. This was 15.2 times higher than in the same period last year, based on activity over the last 30 days. Allaire explained that CPN's payment volume is now more than $58 billion.

Circle also revealed that USDC has now become the leading settlement asset in agentic/automated internet payments. Allaire disclosed that over 99% of agent payments on x402 are settled in USDC.

In the third quarter, Circle's total revenue and reserve income were $865 million, up 17% year-on-year. This figure included $182 million from ARC token sales, according to an image showing Circle's Q3 highlights.

According to Allaire, the impressive performance in the third quarter is a strong signal that Circle is ready for the next phase of stablecoin adoption. He said the GENIUS Act, which is expected to take effect in January, will bring regulated digital dollars into the mainstream. Also, Circle has now activated all the layers of its platform.

The impressive third-quarter data indicates that Circle has not only further solidified USDC's dominance in terms of transaction activity but is also expanding its ecosystem across payments, on-chain finance, and institutional adoption.

Do this: ask an advertising provider for a sample campaign report before you ask for a proposal.

Can you see which audiences converted? Does conversion mean a registration, a wallet connection, or a completed transaction? Can you detect where the ads appeared and spending on placements that aren’t generating results?

These questions will tell you much more than a professionally made slide showing millions of impressions. After all, you are choosing a company to spend your budget, and you need to understand what it intends to buy, how it measures it, and what it changes.

Here is what you should be checking before you commit.

When a provider says it reaches “crypto users,” that’s not enough. Ask what qualifies someone for this label. Is it someone who once read a Bitcoin article, or an active trader who is comparing exchanges right now? Each of these suggests a very different audience.

Here is what a good answer sounds like. Ask Blockchain-Ads, the platform Coinbase, Binance and OKX buy on, and you get a segment with a definition and a recency window: active crypto traders, people who recently compared exchanges or wallets, or your own depositors as a retargeting group. That precision is what a demand-side platform is for, and Blockchain-Ads was the first one built for crypto, iGaming and finance. Hold every network on your shortlist to the same standard.

For example, if you are promoting a lending protocol, your question should be whether you can reach a segment of people interested in DeFi lending, and how recently they showed that interest. Then you should request an audience estimate for your target countries.

When you compare crypto advertising networks, a comparison of crypto ad networks gives you a starting shortlist. Then get specific:

A publisher list will tell you where your ads might appear. It won’t necessarily tell you who will see them.

There are two different buying approaches to understand here:

Let’s say you sell a wallet for active DeFi users. A crypto news placement could reach experienced users alongside casual readers. Audience targeting could reach relevant users while they browse other subjects.

Now here is the trick. Neither approach automatically wins. Your task here is to ask the provider what they support and whether you can apply contextual restrictions when you need them.

The most important test for an advertising network that serves crypto exchanges is whether it can connect the advertising spend to funded accounts and trading activity.

For a wallet, the event could be a completed swap.

For a blockchain game, it could be a player returning after a first session.

Give the provider your event definition and ask the following:

The best crypto advertising network for your project needs to measure the actual outcome.

Tip: A public transaction doesn’t automatically reveal which ad acquired the user. Blockchain-Ads’ attribution guide explains that campaign identifiers must be linked to account or wallet activity.

Start with the conversion definition. Then, examine the headline number.

Ask for evidence that matches your situation: similar product, target market, budget, and conversion event. Then check the following:

Minimum deposits, daily budgets, and service eligibility are separate commitments when you pick a crypto advertising network.

Blockchain-Ads, for example, publishes its minimum deposit and daily budget, and offers a self-serve platform or a managed option run by industry experts.

Ask any provider for the same clarity. You need to be able to confirm management fees, creative costs, top-up requirements, and the treatment of unused funds.

Finally, ask what the proposed budget can reasonably test. You need a clear explanation of how the funds will be split across countries, formats, and audiences.

A total CPA can hide expensive placements behind cheaper ones.

Ask for a demonstration of reporting by audience, creative, country, device, and placement. The idea here is to confirm which breakdowns are available together and which require support or an export request.

Try a very practical question during the demo:

“If mobile conversions drop next week, what can I do to investigate this?”

Ideally, you should be able to examine whether the delivery shifted toward a different audience or country.

Tip: Ask how quickly the reports update, and check whether existing customers can be excluded from acquisition campaigns. Otherwise, a campaign may receive credit for people you already acquired. Remember: the best crypto ads in a presentation are less useful than reporting that helps you decide what deserves your money.

Fraud protection needs much more explanation than a badge on a well-designed website.

Ask what gets filtered before buying, what gets checked afterward, and how you can report suspicious activity. Find out whether you can pause delivery during an investigation and what evidence the provider needs.

Blockchain-Ads, for instance, documents independent impression verification, traffic monitoring, allow and block lists, and frequency controls. It also asks advertisers reporting problems to supply the campaign ID and period.

Use these categories when you talk to providers:

Finally, ask who will review performance and what would trigger a change.

Marko Rendevski, SVP Advertising Services & Partnerships at Blockchain-Ads, describes the principle clearly: “We don’t make decisions based only on CTR or a small number of clicks.”

Have the provider explain how they will assess your campaign against your target conversion cost and normal conversion delay. Someone who deposits several days after registration needs time to appear in the results.

If you are wondering how to choose a crypto ad network, finish it all with this one question:

“What will we know after this first test?”

Choosing a crypto advertising network is not simple. Before you commit, ask the provider to show you how it would build your audience, track your conversions, and report where your money went. Get the costs and the test plan in writing. You should leave that conversation only once you know what the first campaign will test and how you can judge the results.

#5336. Riot Liquidates 79% of Its Bitcoin Treasury for $28 Billion AI Infrastructure Deal

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

American Riot Platforms Inc. (RIOT) sold off 79% of its Bitcoin in the third quarter of 2026, redirecting capital toward building infrastructure for artificial intelligence. According to a fresh financial report, the company reduced its cryptocurrency reserves from 11,380 to 2,418 BTC.

In total, over the first nine months of the year, Riot sold 20,264 BTC on the market, receiving about $1.5 billion for them. This money went toward financing a major technological shift: the company's free energy capacity is being repurposed for high-performance computing needs.

Riot shares reacted to the session open with a sharp jump to $16.20, after which they stabilized in the $15.45–$15.50 range, holding positions on elevated volumes.

The main incentive for selling the cryptocurrency was a 15-year agreement to lease ready-made sites and capacities (powered land lease) totaling 910 MW at the Corsicana campus in Texas. The strategic partner was the Frontier AI Lab (Anthropic) laboratory.

The initial cost of the contract is estimated at $28 billion, and the average annual rent at the start will be about $1.8 billion. Taking into account other projects, Riot's total long-term revenue in the data center segment has reached $38 billion, and the total controlled capacity is 1,151 MW.

Riot CEO Jason Les noted that the agreement is structured as a triple-net lease. Under its terms, the client itself purchases and maintains the computing equipment. For Riot, this reduces construction costs by roughly half compared to standard Tier 3 data centers. As a result, the company will be able to do without issuing new shares and diluting investors' stakes.

The shift in focus is occurring against the backdrop of falling margins in classic mining. Riot's quarterly revenue from cryptocurrency mining fell by 28% — to $116 million, although the company actually mined 1,637 BTC.

Nevertheless, total quarterly revenue held at $181.4 million (+1% year-over-year), outpacing market forecasts. Net profit amounted to $4.03 million.

To optimize its balance sheet, the company fully closed its $200 million credit line with Coinbase, returning 5,821 BTC from collateral. Riot ended the quarter with free liquidity of $950.2 million (including cash and the remainder of the cryptocurrency). The balance sheet retains 2,418 BTC, which may also go under the hammer in the fourth quarter to finance the Texas construction.
